steps: Check opening & hearth
Masonry wood-burning fireplace only, with the minimum opening drawn in Fig. 3. The non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the opening.

The minimum fireplace opening is given only as a drawing (Figure 3); read the dimensions from this page of the PDF.

The rating label (p. 3) adds: install only on a non-combustible hearth under the unit, extending 16 in / 406 mm in front of the fireplace opening face.
Lay ember protection
Protect combustible flooring with non-combustible material: USA 16" to the firing side (from the glass) and 8" to each side of the door opening; Canada 18" and 8" to each side of the unit.

Codes: N.F.P.A. 211 (USA), CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada). Figure 4 shows further dimensions as a drawing only.

Optional leveling legs (bolts) level or steady the insert on an uneven hearth. If the fireplace is lower than the hearth, prop the unit up and thread the supplied bolts into the inserts under the sides toward the rear, set to the depth of the drop.
Hold clearances
From the side of the door: 13 in. to an adjacent sidewall, 9-1/2 in. to side facing (max 3-1/2 in. deep). From the top: 13 in. to mantel facing and to a mantel (max 12 in. deep).
Prepare fireplace & chimney
Sweep and inspect; repair cracks, loose mortar or other defects first. Chimney 15' minimum from hearth and not serving another appliance; lock the damper open or remove it.

• Fireplace and chimney must suit wood burning; the masonry fireplace must be built to N.F.P.A. 211 or applicable codes, and the installation must conform to CAN/CSA-B365.
  • Do not remove bricks or mortar. Exception: masonry or steel, including the damper plate, may be removed from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame to fit a liner, if that doesn't weaken the fireplace and chimney or reduce protection for combustibles below the National Building Code.
  • If the fireplace was modified for the insert, fasten the supplied metal tag to the back wall of the fireplace.
  • Two people to install. Put cardboard or a heavy blanket on the hearth. Never a makeshift or temporary installation.
Confirm factory-built fireplaces: the rating label (p. 3) and this page (p. 16) say the insert must not be installed in a factory-built fireplace; the Clearances text on p. 15 refers to installation "into a masonry or factory built fireplace", and the contents (p. 2) list an "Into a Factory Built Fireplace" section that the manual doesn't contain.
Run the liner

Full stainless liner from the flue collar to the chimney top (required in Canada: class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635, or CAN/ULC-S640) with a stove-to-liner adapter. USA only: direct flue connection into the first flue tile, throat sealed.

Full liner: measure the chimney height from the top of the existing flue to the hearth floor (this allows extra liner for flashing and rain cap). Feed the stainless steel liner from the top of the chimney, through the damper area into the fireplace cavity, and attach a "stove to liner" adapter per the liner maker's instructions.

Direct flue connection (USA only, p. 18): measure from the top of the first flue liner tile to the top of the insert, allowing extra to enter the tile. Feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile, attach the adapter, and seal where the liner passes through the chimney throat. A clean-out door may be required by local codes. Then follow full-liner steps 3-9.

Pacific Energy highly recommends the full liner as the safest installation with optimum performance: it drafts correctly and prevents difficult start-ups and smoking out the door.
Collar, set & level

Fix the 6" I.D. collar to the adapter with three stainless screws and high temp stove cement; push the insert in and level it. Remove the baffle, pull the collar down through the flue opening with the tool, clamp, center and tighten.

The flue collar is packaged in the stove; make sure its gasket is in good shape. Leveling-leg nuts are in the bottom sides, front and rear. Pull the collar down until its bolts pass through the mounting slots, fit the clamps and nuts, center the collar on the opening and tighten.

Re-install the baffle assembly in reverse order (p. 11): side blanket insulation tight against the side rails, ceramic board pushed back tight against the baffle.

Do not operate with the baffle assembly, tubes or insulation removed.
Flashing & rain cap
Measure, trim and shape a chimney-top flashing for a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side; seat it over the liner, firmly against the flue tile. Attach a rain cap; a storm collar is optional.
Combustion air
Outside air: replace the ash clean-out cover with a rodent screen, keep the air inlet uncovered and seal the surround to the fireplace face. Otherwise the unit draws room air through its bottom.
Blower power
Properly grounded three-prong outlet; never cut or remove the grounding prong. Route the cord away from hot or sharp surfaces and never under the unit; wire to local codes, ANSI/NFPA 70 or CSA C22.2.
Fit the surround

Bolt panels A, B and C together face-down with the 1/4" x 1/2" bolts at points D; stand it up and check the face is flat. Slide it over the unit and ash shelf into the bracket slots, then push back to the fireplace face.

Regular surroundA 37" / 965mm · B 28" / 710mm
Oversized surroundA 42" / 1070mm · B 30" / 760mm

Sizes from p. 12 (A and B as lettered in that drawing). Parts: standard surround 11250045, oversized 11250037. With outside air, seal the surround to the fireplace face once installed (p. 19).

Door gasket leakage → replace gasket, check latch

items: Fire too small → build a larger fire
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean

items: Air control set too high → set it lower
Not enough wood → unsplit wood is preferred
Draft too high → excessive chimney height and/or diameter
Door gasket leaking → replace door gasket

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build every fire right on the firebricks. Never use a grate or andirons to raise the wood.

  1. Move the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the middle of the firebox. Crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it, then add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame. Don't leave the insert unattended while the door is open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. When there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air for normal burning.
No liquid starters. Never use gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire, and keep them well away from the insert. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine.

Your first few fires

The paint bakes on during the first 2-3 fires. Ventilate the room well and open all windows and doors: the smoke and fumes can bother some people. Follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with the insert. Smoke detectors may go off more often for a while. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Setting the air control
air.html:
The air control runs from High "H" (all the way to the left), the maximum firing rate, to Low "L" (pushed to the far right). Use High only to start a fire or to get a fresh load going.

  • After each load, leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes, when most of the smoke is made. After 30 minutes or so you can turn it down a lot without making excess smoke.
  • Smoke pouring down across the glass (a "waterfall") means you turned the air down too soon, or too low.
  • Every home's heating needs differ, so the right setting takes trial and error. Note what works for next time.
  • Wood type, outside temperature, chimney size and weather all change the right setting.
Don't over-fire. A glowing red top or vent pipe means the fire is too hot. Over-firing can permanently damage the insert and chimney, and may void the warranty.
The insert has a factory-set minimum burn rate. Changing it is against federal regulations, and the air control must never be altered: tampering voids the warranty and can be very hazardous.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
Adding wood

  1. Move the air control to high and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. This stops smoke puffing back into the room.
  3. Load the logs endwise, placed so air can flow between them. Always use dry wood.
  4. Don't load so high, or in such a way, that opening the door would be hazardous. Make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close the door.

Small loads burn cleanest: two or three logs at a time, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load.

Overnight burns

Unsplit logs work best. Char the wood completely on the maximum setting before turning the air down for the night. Never try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting from embers

  1. Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front. Put a couple of dry, split logs on top and close the door.
  2. Set the air to high. The logs should start burning in a few minutes.
  3. Once the wood has charred, reset the air where you like it.
Fire not lasting the night? The usual causes: air set too high, not enough wood, too much chimney draft, or a leaking door gasket.

wood.title: Choosing and testing your wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only: seasoned cordwood. Air-dried, seasoned hardwoods give higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwoods or green, freshly cut hardwoods.

  • Air-dry (season) wood for six months or more, and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Test a piece

Add a large piece to a good, large bed of coals. Dry: it burns on more than one side within one minute. Damp: it turns black and lights within three minutes. Soaked: it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Salt-water wood, treated wood, wet or green wood, coal or charcoal, garbage, solvents, yard waste, railroad ties, manure, anything containing rubber, plastic or asbestos, building debris, petroleum products, paints or asphalt, or paper, cardboard, plywood or particleboard. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that quickly destroy metal and void the warranty.

Confirm log length: the manual gives 17 inches maximum (16 inches ideal) on p. 3, and up to 18" on p. 7.

blower.title: Running the blowers
blower.html:
Two blowers sit under the ash shelf at the front of the insert. You run them with an on/off rocker switch and a fan speed control.

Rocker switch offAutomatic: the blowers come on once the insert reaches operating temperature, and shut off after the fire is out and it has cooled
Rocker switch onManual: bypasses the temperature switch for full control

In either mode, set the fan speed control where you want it.

Suggested settings

  • Air control on "L" (low, pushed to the far right): run the blowers on low.
  • Air control anywhere above "L": any blower speed you like.

Keep them clean

At least every six months, vacuum the grill openings on the back and bottom of the blower casing. Vacuum the front grill to clear dust and pet hair.

The blowers need a properly grounded outlet that takes a three-prong plug. Never cut or remove the grounding prong, and unplug the insert before any service.

glass.title: Glass & door care
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the insert is cold, with fireplace glass cleaner. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that could scratch.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion and dry, seasoned wood, so your pipes and chimney are fairly clean. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. That buildup is forming at least as fast in your chimney.

Other causes of dirty glass: turning the air down too soon, too little chimney draft, or a leaking door gasket.

Protect the glass

  • Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close it.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the insert again. Use only 10-1/2" x 16-1/2" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.

Door and gasket

  • Clean the plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.
  • Check the door gasket weekly for sagging, placement and damage. Replace it when needed with the gasket kit (prt# 80000670).

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out only when the insert is cold.

  • When the ash gets 3" to 4" deep, wait until the fire has burned down and cooled, then remove the excess.
  • Leave an ash bed about 1" deep on the firebox floor. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Keep the front of the firebox clear of heavy ash. That's where boost air for the fire comes in.

Getting rid of ashes

Put them in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn, until final disposal. If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all cinders have thoroughly cooled. Don't put any other waste in that container.

While the firebox is cold and empty, look over the firebricks for cracks (the manual suggests weekly). Replace broken or missing bricks: burning without them can create a hazardous condition.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney cleaning
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires give off tar and vapours that condense in the cool chimney as creosote. If creosote catches fire, it burns extremely hot. Some creosote is unavoidable; regular inspection and cleaning is the answer.

How often

  • Have the chimney connector and chimney inspected at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Check daily until experience shows how often you need to clean. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months, when burning rates are higher.

Keep buildup down

  • Burn dry, seasoned wood with plenty of air.
  • Burn small loads, and leave the air open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading.
  • Black, greasy glass is an early warning: the same deposit is building in the chimney.
Pacific Energy recommends professionals certified by a qualified agency, such as the National Fireplace Institute or the Chimney Safety Institute of America. If the baffle assembly comes out for cleaning, it must go back in: never run the insert with the baffle, its tubes or insulation removed.

safety.title: Safety & chimney fires
safety.html:
Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get ready to evacuate. Have a plan everyone understands, and a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air control on the insert.
  3. Call the fire department. Have a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Once it's out, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks before you light another fire. Check combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.

Every day

  • The insert is hot while it runs. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning. Open it only to add wood.
  • Keep stored wood, furniture, newspapers and other loose combustibles out of the clearance area and the space you need for loading.
  • Burn wood only. Charcoal and other fuels can make large amounts of carbon monoxide, an odourless gas that can kill. Never barbecue in the insert.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended near the insert.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's Limited Lifetime Wood Products Warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years)Parts only: porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part, from the date of purchase, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Never warranted: firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets.
  • Left out of the lifetime coverage: firebox rails and heat shields. Labor isn't covered under the lifetime warranty.
  • Any part showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Early deterioration usually points to improper use, such as excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals), and may void the warranty. Pacific Energy recommends a certified installer.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, the model name and the serial number. You can register the insert at pacificenergy.net/register; the serial number is on the certification label or the manual cover.

specOutput.title: Heat output
specOutput.html:
EPA Btu output13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr
Rating label statement13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr

The output range is based on CSA B415 efficiency and burn rates from the low and high EPA tests using Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. The label statement gives the range shown under specific test conditions (2020 EPA crib wood limits, Method 28R).

specEmis.title: Emissions & efficiency
specEmis.html:
EPA certified emissions1.9 grams per hour
HHV tested efficiency72%
LHV tested efficiency78%

Meets the 2020 U.S. EPA crib wood particulate emission standards, tested with Method 28R. Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415: LHV assumes the fuel moisture is already vapour; HHV includes the energy needed to vaporize the water in the fuel.

The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered; doing so is against federal regulations (p. 7).

specWood.title: Wood length & fuel
specWood.html:
Maximum wood length17 inches
Ideal wood length16 inches
FuelSeasoned cord wood

Build the fire directly on the firebrick; no grate or andirons. Load endwise.

Confirm maximum log length: the manual gives 17 inches (ideal 16 inches) in the rating information on p. 3, and "up to 18"(457mm)" in Normal Operation on p. 7.

specFlue.title: Flue, liner & chimney
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D., removable
CanadaFull liner required: class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635, or CAN/ULC-S640
USAFlue liner to UL-1777, or direct flue connection
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)
Recommended flue draft.06" w.c. – .09" w.c., hot, on high

The full liner runs continuous from the flue collar to the top of the chimney; Pacific Energy highly recommends it as the safest installation with optimum performance. A direct flue connection (USA only, p. 18) runs the liner into the first flue tile with a seal in the chimney throat; local codes may require a clean-out door. Never connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.

Excessive draft shows as an uncontrollable burn or glowing red stove part or chimney; inadequate draft as back puffing or smoke leaking at appliance and connector joints (p. 8).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Minimum clearances to combustibles, measured from the side of the door and from the insert top.

Side of door to adjacent sidewall13 in.
Side of door to side facing (max 3-1/2 in. deep)9-1/2 in.
Top to mantel facing13 in.
Top to mantel (max 12 in. deep)13 in.

The rating label (p. 3) gives the same inch values. Figure 5 on this page shows them as a drawing.

Confirm the metric clearances: the rating label on p. 3 gives 330 mm (sidewall), 240 mm (side facing), 330 mm (top facing) and 330 mm (mantel); the table on p. 15 gives 255 mm, 155 mm, 305 mm and 305 mm for the same inch values.
Confirm factory-built fireplaces: p. 15 says these clearances apply when installed into "a masonry or factory built fireplace"; the rating label (p. 3) and Installation section (p. 16) say the insert must not be installed in a factory-built fireplace.

specHearth.title: Hearth & ember protection
specHearth.html:
Masonry hearth (non-combustible)16" in front, 8" beyond each side of the fireplace opening
Ember protection, U.S.A.16" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the door opening
Ember protection, Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the unit

Ember protection is non-combustible material over combustible flooring in front of the insert; codes are CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada) and N.F.P.A. 211 (USA). The hearth requirement is on p. 13; the rating label (p. 3) says to install only on a non-combustible hearth under the unit, extending 16 in / 406 mm in front of the fireplace opening face.

The minimum fireplace opening (Figure 3, p. 13) and further ember-protection dimensions (Figure 4, this page) are shown only as drawings; take them from the PDF.

specElec.title: Electrical & blowers
specElec.html:
Rating label (p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP
Blowers section (p. 20)120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A
Confirm the voltage: the manual gives 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP on the rating label (p. 3) and 120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A in the Blowers section (p. 20).

Two circulating air blowers under the ash shelf: thermostatically controlled, with a manual bypass rocker switch and a fan speed control. Use only a properly grounded outlet that accepts a three-pronged plug; don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Route the cord away from hot or sharp surfaces, never under the unit. Wire to local codes, or else CSA C22.2 (Canada) / National Electrical Code ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA). Disconnect power before servicing.

Blower box removal: unplug, remove the screw on each side of the blower box under the ash shelf, then pull the blower box / ash shelf assembly forward, tilting it to pass over the primary air control. Reverse to install without bending the primary air control. Parts: blowers 80002623 (RHS) and 80002624 (LHS), wire harness 80002862.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Outside airThrough the fireplace ash clean-out: cover removed, rodent screen in its place
Room airDrawn in through the bottom of the unit

Consult local building codes on combustion air supply. For outside air, don't cover the air inlet opening when setting the insert; when installation is complete, seal the surround to the fireplace face and anywhere else air may enter, so combustion air is drawn from outside into the intake on the bottom of the appliance.

If the stove won't burn, the troubleshooting chart says to check the outside air supply for obstruction and that the room air cover is removed (p. 22).

conflicts.issue: Maximum wood length: 17 inches (16 inches ideal) in the rating/efficiency information vs 'up to 18"(457mm)' in Normal Operation. Also flagged in the owner 'wood' drawer.
Electrical rating: 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP on the rating label vs 120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A in the Blowers section.

Metric clearances: rating label gives 330 mm / 240 mm / 330 mm / 330 mm (sidewall / side facing / top facing / mantel); the p. 15 table gives 255 mm / 155 mm / 305 mm / 305 mm for the same 13 / 9-1/2 / 13 / 13 in. The inch values agree.

Factory-built fireplaces: rating label and Installation section say not to install in a factory-built fireplace; the Clearances text says the clearances apply 'when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace', and the contents page lists an 'Into a Factory Built Fireplace' section that the manual doesn't contain. Also shown in the step3 drawer.

review.notes: Single manual (32 pp.; pp. 29-31 blank). No French-only or scrambled text; the rating label is bilingual and only its English was used. Not transcribed because they exist only as unlabeled drawing callouts: overall unit dimensions (Fig. 2, p. 12), the minimum fireplace opening (Fig. 3, p. 13), the extra ember-protection callouts in Fig. 4 (p. 14; its 'CAN 18" / 406mm' pairs Canada's 18" with the USA's 406 mm, while the label gives 457 MM / 18 IN), the 34 3/8" callout in Fig. 5 (p. 15), the firebrick layout (pp. 23-25) and the parts diagram (p. 27); the guide points to those pages. Cross-reference slips: p. 16 says the fireplace minimum size is on page 12 (it is on p. 13); p. 13 cites a 'Figure 23' that doesn't exist; p. 15 cites Figure 4 for clearances (the clearance drawing is Figure 5). EPA output appears as 13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr (efficiency table) and 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr (label statement), both on p. 3; both shown, treated as rounding rather than a conflict. Surround sizes (p. 12) shown as printed: 'A 37" / 965mm' - 965 mm does not match 37" (the other surround values match their mm). Warranty heading reads 'LTD Lifetime Coverage (10 years)'; shown as printed. Catalog fields the manual doesn't state, so neither used nor compared: heating area, maximum cordwood output, firebox volume, weight, blower cfm, viewing area, non-catalytic combustion. All checkable catalog specs (EPA output, 72% HHV, 1.9 g/hr, 17/16 in. wood length, 6 in. flue) match p. 3/p. 12, though p. 7's 18" wood length disagrees (flagged as a conflict). Catalog says 'Not for sale in the USA'; this is the US edition, certified for Canada and U.S.A. The manual doesn't cover power outages.
